newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela 1996 GDP seen down 1.6 pct - Central Bank.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela 1996 GDP seen down 1.6 pct - Central Bank.

text.p: Venezuela's economy is expected to fall by 1.6 percent of gross domestic product in 1996, according to the Central Bank's annual year-end review of the Venezuelan economy.
While the non-oil economy is seen shrinking 3.6 percent in the year "the oil sector has continued the dynamism of recent years growing an estimated 4.9 percent," the Central Bank document said.
Difficult macroeconomic conditions at the start of 1996, followed by the IMF-sponsored economic adjustment program in mid-April, saw aggregate internal fall an estimated 5.0 percent, the Bank said.

That fall was reflected in estimated drops of 6.0 percent in public consumption, 4.0 percent in private consumption and 7.2 percent in gross fixed investment. Investment rates "have maintained the weakness of recent years, primarily by the private sector whose contraction is seen at around 32.8 percent," the bank said citing price and foreign exchange controls at the start of the year as the principal deterrents.
